title: Outdoor STEM Challenge Cards Volume 2
tagline: 24 new engineering challenges · Fair testing · Simple machines
goal: 24 brand-new outdoor building challenges, none repeated from Volume 1 (and you don't need Volume 1). Your kid makes rope from grass, launches pinecones, moves water uphill, catches the wind and moves a too-heavy rock with a stick, testing fairly and measuring every time.
need: These cards, on your phone or printed and cut out
Fallen natural materials: sticks, rocks, leaves, pinecones, sand
Everyday things: string, cups, foil, rubber bands, a spoon

lesson.text: Volume 2 is about fair testing: change one thing at a time, and measure. Then you know what made the difference.
lesson.before: We tried a bunch of stuff and it went farther.

model.line: Does a longer launcher arm send the pinecone farther?
Same pinecone, same pull, same spot on the ground.
Only the arm: a short stick, then a long one.
Short arm: 4 steps. Long arm: 7 steps. Tried 3 times each.

lesson.modelNote: That's card 5, Fair Test Flight. When your kid changes three things at once, ask: which one made the difference? Change one, and test again.

howTo.intro: No science background needed. You're the measurer and the fair-test referee: hold them to changing one thing at a time. Use only fallen materials, keep water challenges to puddles, basins or a sink, and take builds apart when you're done.

plan.what: Pick a theme, or 3 to 5 cards, and pack string, cups and foil.
Plan, build, test, improve, measuring every try. About 15 to 30 minutes each.
Note the best result, then take builds apart and leave the space as you found it.

troubleshoot.a: Ask which one change made the difference. Then go back and change just that one thing.

troubleshoot.q: Results are all over the place
troubleshoot.a: Test 3 times and use the middle result. Real scientists repeat tests too.

levelsLine: Three levels on every card. Explore: do the challenge. Develop: add the Deeper part. Extend: test 3 times, write the results down, and explain what made the difference.

cards.name: Rope Maker
cards.t: Twist dry grass or long leaves into a cord as long as your arm.
cards.d: Make a thicker cord. Which one holds more weight before snapping?

cards.name: Lash It Tight
cards.t: Join two sticks into a solid X, using only string.
cards.d: Lash 3 sticks into a triangle. Why is it harder to bend?

cards.name: The Hanging Test
cards.t: Tie a stick between two supports with a different knot on each end. Which knot slips first?
cards.d: Learn one real knot and test again. What made it stronger?

cards.name: The Carrier
cards.t: Weave string between two sticks to make a stretcher that carries a load of pinecones.
cards.d: How loose can the weave get before the load falls through?

cards.name: Pulley Lift
cards.t: Loop a string over a low, strong branch and use it to lift a small bag of stones.
cards.d: Is pulling down easier than lifting up? Why do you think so?

cards.name: Fair Test Flight
cards.t: Build a simple launcher (sticks, a rubber band, a spoon). Launch the same object 5 times and measure each flight.
cards.d: Results different? Find what you accidentally changed, and fix it.

cards.name: Angle Hunter
cards.t: Launch at a low, a middle and a high angle. Which one sends your object farthest?
cards.d: Predict a new angle's distance before you launch. How close were you?

cards.name: Target Tuner
cards.t: Set a target two steps away. Adjust one thing at a time until you hit it 3 times in a row.
cards.d: Move the target farther. Which change moves the landing spot most?

cards.name: Payload Problem
cards.t: Launch a light, a medium and a heavy object with the same pull. Measure all three.
cards.d: Find the heaviest object that still clears a one-step line.

cards.name: Stone Skipper
cards.t: On calm, shallow water with a grown-up, find the stone shape that skips the most times.
cards.d: Change one thing (the throw angle, the stone, the speed). Which matters most?

cards.name: The Aqueduct
cards.t: Move water from one cup to another a step away without carrying it. Build a channel from foil, straws or bark.
cards.d: Rebuild it to spill less. Measure how much you lose.

cards.name: Uphill Problem
cards.t: Now the empty cup sits higher. Move the water anyway, without carrying the cups.
cards.d: Time your ideas. Which moves the most water per minute?

cards.name: Splitter
cards.t: Build one channel that fills two cups at once from a single pour.
cards.d: Make the split unfair on purpose: two thirds and one third.

cards.name: The Leak Patrol
cards.t: A partner secretly adds 3 leaks to your channel. Find them and patch them all.
cards.d: Patch with a leaf, foil or mud. Which survives a second pour?

cards.name: Water Wheel
cards.t: Build a small wheel from a stick and leaves or spoons that spins when you pour water over it.
cards.d: Add more paddles, or fewer. Which spins fastest?

cards.name: Slow Fall
cards.t: Build a parachute that doubles a pinecone's fall time from shoulder height.
cards.d: Test two canopy sizes. When does bigger stop helping?

cards.name: Wind Spinner
cards.t: Build a paper spinner that turns in the wind without flying off its stick.
cards.d: Add cup-shaped blades and count turns in 10 seconds. That's an anemometer.

cards.name: Sail Power
cards.t: Attach a sail to something that rolls or slides. Move it one step with wind or your breath.
cards.d: Race two sail shapes: tall and narrow against short and wide.

cards.name: Wind Finder
cards.t: Build a wind vane: a light arrow on a stick that shows where the wind comes from.
cards.d: Check the direction 3 times today. Does your wind have a favourite?

cards.name: Leaf Kite
cards.t: Tie a string to a big, sturdy leaf and get it to fly on a breezy day.
cards.d: Move where the string is tied. Which spot makes it fly highest?

cards.name: Rock Mover
cards.t: Move a too-heavy rock with a stick lever over a pivot stone. Try the pivot near, then far.
cards.d: In the easy setup you push farther but lighter. That's the lever's trade.

cards.name: Ramp vs Lift
cards.t: Get a heavy stone onto a ledge two ways: lifted straight up, and rolled up a ramp.
cards.d: A short steep ramp or a long gentle one: what does the long one cost?

cards.name: Two-Machine Combo
cards.t: Chain a ramp and a lever together. Move a stone through both in one go.
cards.d: Draw your machine and mark the push, the pivot and the load.

cards.name: The Stick Scale
cards.t: Hang a stick by its middle with a cup on each end. Use your scale to compare two objects.
cards.d: Slide one cup inward so a light object balances a heavy one.

conclusion.headline: Your kid just ran real experiments.
conclusion.text: They built, tested, measured, and changed one thing at a time until they knew exactly what made the difference. Fair testing, forces and simple machines, learned with sticks, string and water.
conclusion.celebrate: Point to a number: 'Your long arm sent it 7 steps instead of 4.' Measuring their own improvement is what makes it stick.
extensions: Pick the best design from each theme and run a family championship
Keep a results notebook: card, what changed, what you measured
Combine three machines into one long chain reaction

signs: They change one thing at a time without being reminded
They measure instead of saying 'it's better'
They spot levers, ramps and pulleys in everyday life
makeItReal: Find a real job for a simple machine: move a heavy log with a lever, get a wheelbarrow up a step with a ramp, lift a bucket into a treehouse with a pulley. When the machine does real work, kids feel the physics.
cta: Want the next one? This guide is one of 120+ in the Anywhere Learning library, each with your job and your kid's job at every step.
